raw_case_text: These two patients were siblings. Case 1 was the elder brother, a full-term boy with a birth weight of 2.8 kg and congenital heart defects (coarctation of the aorta, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus). He underwent a cardiac operation at the age of 1 month and also developed neonatal jaundice. He presented with recurrent cough, wheezing, and tachypnea beginning at 2 months. He has also experienced developmental delay, recurrent diarrhea, feeding problems, and poor weight gain from the age of 2 months. During illness, he needed nasogastric feeding but was fed orally after discharge. He had two episodes of respiratory exacerbations accompanied by respiratory failure, leading to hospitalizations at the ages of 3 and 8 months. During his first hospitalization at 3 months, a physical examination revealed crackles, wheezing, retractions, funnel chest, hypotonia, and poor visual contact. His respiratory rate was 60-90 times/min, and his oxygen saturation (SpO2) was 80%-92%, requiring oxygen supplementation. He was anemic (hemoglobin 73 g/L), and his liver function indicators were slightly elevated [alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 53 U/L, total bilirubin (TBIL) 22 mumol/L]. His white blood cell count, C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), renal function, and thyroid function tests were within normal ranges. Pneumocystis jirovecii were found in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Immunological work-up showed a mild decrease in IgG and IgA levels, while lymphocyte subtypes remained normal. A chest CT showed bilateral ground-glass opacities (GGOs) and consolidations at the age of 3 months (Figure 1A). He developed respiratory failure necessitating invasive ventilation for 6 days and received anti-infection treatment for 1 month, with multiple antibiotics including trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole for P. jirovecii and antifungal drugs. He also received prednisone at a daily dose of 0.75 mg/kg for 20 days. After 1 month, repeated chest CT showed little improvement. After discharge, his cough improved, but tachypnea and oxygen desaturation persisted (respiratory rate 50-60 times/min, SpO2 94%). At the age of 8 months, he presented with a short-term fever followed by another episode of respiratory failure. Multiple pathogens were found in the aspiration of sputum obtained from the oropharynx, nasal cavity, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid during the second hospitalization, including Staphylococcus aureus, Moraxella catarrhalis, Candida parapsilosis, rhinovirus, and human metapneumovirus. The repeated chest CT indicated GGOs in the same area as before and increased consolidations (Figure 1B). Unfortunately, despite anti-infection treatment, he died of respiratory failure at the age of 8 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 3-month-old full-term male infant with repaired congenital heart disease presented with recurrent cough, wheezing, and tachypnea since 2 months of age that progressed to acute respiratory failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born full-term (birth weight 2.8 kg) with complex congenital heart defects surgically repaired at 1 month of age, the infant developed persistent cough, wheezing, tachypnea, developmental delay, recurrent diarrhea, feeding difficulties requiring intermittent nasogastric tube feeding, and poor weight gain starting at 2 months of age. He suffered two severe respiratory exacerbations with acute respiratory failure requiring hospitalization at 3 months and 8 months of age.
subjective.past_medical_history: Congenital heart defects (coarctation of the aorta, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus) status post surgical repair at 1 month of age; neonatal jaundice; developmental delay, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, recurrent diarrhea, and failure to thrive since 2 months of age. Sibling (younger brother, Case 2 in family) affected by the same genetic syndrome.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent cough, wheezing, tachypnea, dyspnea/retractions, poor visual contact, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, recurrent diarrhea, and poor weight gain.

objective.physical_examination: At 3-month hospitalization: Tachypnea with respiratory rate 60–90 breaths/min, hypoxemia with SpO2 80%–92% (persisting at RR 50–60/min and SpO2 94% post-discharge), chest retractions, pectus excavatum (funnel chest), bilateral pulmonary crackles and wheezing, generalized hypotonia, and poor visual contact.
objective.routine_investigations: At 3-month hospitalization: Anemia with hemoglobin 73 g/L; mildly elevated liver enzymes with ALT 53 U/L and total bilirubin 22 μmol/L; normal WBC count, C-reactive protein (CRP), ESR, renal function, and thyroid function; mild decrease in serum IgG and IgA levels. At 8-month hospitalization: Oropharyngeal, nasal, and BAL fluid aspirates detected Staphylococcus aureus, Moraxella catarrhalis, Candida parapsilosis, rhinovirus, and human metapneumovirus.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunological phenotyping: Normal peripheral lymphocyte subsets. Chest CT at 3 months: Bilateral ground-glass opacities (GGOs) and consolidations (which showed minimal improvement after 1 month of therapy and worsened consolidation at 8 months). Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) examination at 3 months: Positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP; confirmed in BALF at 3 months of age) and chronic childhood interstitial lung disease / syndromic immunodeficiency with developmental delay, hypotonia, and congenital heart defects, complicated at 8 months of age by polymicrobial respiratory infection (Staphylococcus aureus, Moraxella catarrhalis, Candida parapsilosis, rhinovirus, and human metapneumovirus). Plan and clinical course: During his first hospitalization at 3 months, he required invasive mechanical ventilation for 6 days, 1 month of antimicrobial therapy including trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) and antifungals, and oral prednisone (0.75 mg/kg/day for 20 days). Although his cough improved and he was discharged, baseline tachypnea (50–60 breaths/min), hypoxemia (SpO2 94%), and bilateral GGOs persisted. At 8 months of age, he was readmitted with fever, polymicrobial pneumonia, and progressive consolidation on chest CT, and died of refractory respiratory failure.
